rows: Snow White feels that conditions are not ideal, so she calls off today's expedition and returns to her post.

Snow White approaches the forest.
Despite the seemingly endless, internecine conflict between man and Raptures, the forest remains a bastion of life.
As Snow White gazes upon the forest...

*Rustle*

"?!!"

...a deer suddenly leaps into view.

Tendrils of flame belch out of the anti-ship rifle's muzzle. However, as the flames die down, the deer is nowhere to be found. 
The shot also attracts Raptures, and Snow White is forced into a confrontation.

Tendrils of flame belch out of the rifle's muzzle, and the deer is blown apart in a burst of arterial spray.
It's only then that Snow White realizes how fragile a deer is.

The sounds of the battle only attract more Raptures.
It takes everything for Snow White to subdue the threat. In the end, she goes back to the post empty-handed.
Having newly discovered the fragility of ungulates, Snow White decides to walk around the woods and find alternative hunting tools.

On the right, the ground is covered with mushrooms that have brilliant red patterns.
Snow White begins to pick the mushrooms.

Walking forward, Snow White discovers a wooden cabin.
She heads inside to look for any useful items.

On the left, Snow White sees a chain link fence.
She walks towards it, intending to snip it into separate parts that could be used to make traps.
She wonders if she should do a taste test before bringing them to her colleagues.

Snow White feels somewhat hesitant about sharing food with others that hasn't been tested. 
She puts a mushroom in her mouth.
Snow White feels that the mushrooms are bad news, so she puts them down <color=#20B2AA>and heads out of the forest.</color>

Suddenly, a white fog envelops her.
A female figure can be made out amongst the fog. 
It is someone whose face she has longed to see for some time.

"Snow White."

Someone calls out.

"!!!"

Snow White opens her eyes.
The white fog has dissipated.
After making sure she hasn't sustained any injuries, Snow White realizes something.
The mushroom she ate made her hallucinate.

Snow White contemplates if she should eat the mushroom again.
Although she can't explain why exactly, she wants to see that woman in her hallucination again.
After hesitating for a while, Snow White decides to...

After ingesting some more of the mushrooms, Snow White sees two flowers amidst the fog.

One is white, and the other is red.
Which one should she follow?
No matter how badly she wants to see that woman, falling into a hallucination is a risky proposition. She puts the mushrooms down and <color=#20B2AA>heads out of the forest.</color>

Snow White heads toward the white flower and sees a white figure.
The faceless figure asks, 

"Can you see me?"

Snow White heads toward the red flower and hears the buzz of a radio.
An old song is being played. Someone can be heard humming along to the song. They sound homesick.

*Thud* *Crash*

Snow White stumbles over a tree stump and tumbles to the ground.

"!!!"

After waking up from her hallucination, Snow White still wants to see that face that may or may not be a figment of her imagination, so she eats some mushrooms again.

No matter how many mushrooms Snow White ingests, the face she longs to see remains forever indistinct.
Snow White spends the entire day lost in meaningless reveries.
If you're not yet ready, try following the other flower.

The white figure smiles.
"If you want to see me, you should come to meet me."
"Snow White."

*Thud*

"!!!"

Snow White opens her eyes.
A towering tree stands before her.
Something about this all seems oddly familiar. Snow White looks at her feet.
As she does, a long-forgotten memory comes rushing back.

On a day when the fighting had no end in sight,
she came over with a memory capsule and a sheet of paper.

"Everyone, write down your wishes on these and place them in this memory capsule."

They tore the sheet of paper into seven pieces, wrote down their wishes, and placed them in the capsule.
She buried the memory capsule in the ground and spoke.

"One day... When our job is finished, let's open it together."

Under that enormous tree, she made a promise that would never come true.

Snow White takes out the time capsule buried in the ground.
There are seven pieces of paper inside.

"..."

"I wish for the war to end and for everyone to make it out safely."
"The day my role doth end, with the red flower shall I go."
"I wish that the day would come when everyone knows our names."
"I want to have food and booze from my hometown!"
"We will win."
"I hope Lilith will be safe."
After reading six pieces of paper, Snow White opens the last one, which has been neatly folded.
It's hers.

"I hope we can save humanity."

"..."

Snow White ponders over the last words she ever wrote.

"I hope we can save humanity..."

Snow White places the pieces of paper back into the capsule and stands up.
To commemorate her, Snow White decides to go to the meadow where she is buried.

Suddenly, a long-forgotten memory comes rushing back to her.
She used to listen to songs with Red Hood, who loved old songs.

"Hello, little one."

Snow White was in a terrible mood that day.
So many of those close to her had lost their lives.
Snow White could never forget their eyes as they died; filled with fear and a hint of relief.
As the music continues to play, Snow White walks up to Red Hood.

"Why do you look so solemn, little one?"
"You're going to give yourself wrinkles if you keep scrunching up your face like that."

Red Hood says with a grin.

"Stop doing that. Take a look at this."

Red Hood brings the radio closer.
It is playing a song about missing one's hometown.
It's an old guitar-centric pop song, which didn't suit the battlefield at all.

"This song is nice, right? This is what music is all about."

Red Hood attempts to coax Snow White,

"Want to try singing it?"

Did Snow White sing with her back then?
She can't remember.

"That's more like it, you dork!"
"... You act like an old geezer."
"Haha! Really?"

Red Hood's laughter and the music are the only sounds that linger in Snow White's ears.

*Thud* *Crash*
Snow White trips over a tree stump.

"!!!"

She wakes up from her hallucination and sees a tent, a broken radio, and a cassette tape near the tree stump that she tripped over.

"..."

Snow White keeps the cassette tape and begins humming the song she heard in her hallucination.

"Oh, the hometown I long for."
"The friends I miss."
"Even if the sky above us is forever grey,"
"We'll return to our hometown someday."

The cabin is entirely bereft of food and supplies. 
However, Snow White can ascertain from the antlers hanging on the wall and the bear skin on the floor that a hunter resided here.

Scrawled directly on the table in red are the words "Don't be the prey."
<color=#20B2AA>Snow White turns and heads back into the forest.</color>

She approaches a metal fence and sees a corpse draped over the top of it. The body is clothed in a camouflage outfit and carrying a bow and backpack.

"..."
Snow White cuts down the metal fence and sets the corpse on the floor.

The duffel bag contains electrical wires, a phone,
dry rations, a pail, and a map.
Snow White looks at the bow & arrow. These weapons, along with the camouflage, might prove useful for hunting. She contemplates whether she should take them.
Snow White doesn't want her survival to come at the expense of someone else's life, so she decides to put down all the hunting props and leave.

Snow White apologizes and takes the dry food, bow & arrow, and camouflage outfit.
She must survive for the sake of her colleagues. If that means benefiting from someone else's death, then so be it.

Snow White prepares to hunt. She starts to set up a trap using the metal wire she got from the fence.
Being proficient with crafting, she succeeds in making a trap and resumes her hunting once again.

Snow White returns to the spot where she saw the deer and sets the trap.
The bleats of a deer can be heard in the distance. She decides to hide behind a tree and watch.

To conceal herself, Snow White...

The unwieldy camouflage does not fool the deer.
Just as it is about to approach the trap, it widens its eyes and flees the scene.
Snow White watches in desperation as the escaping deer slowly disappears into the distance.

No matter how long Snow White waits in hiding, the deer doesn't return.
The trap she made only manages to catch a few small woodland critters. 
With the small animals in tow, Snow White trudges back toward the post.
An Escaped Deer Does Not Return
One needs to be well-prepared to catch a deer.

The deer is fooled by Snow White's camouflage and comes closer.
The moment its foot is clamped by the trap, Snow White shoots it with an arrow.

Snow White captures the deer.
Looking forward to the delicious dinner she'll be having that night, she returns to the post in good spirits.

Scarlet appears before Snow White, who's on her way to explore the river bank.

"Dost thou intend on rusticating by the riverside? Prithee, allow me to accompany you."

Snow White nods.
Scarlet is excited about getting to see some fish, which she hasn't seen in a while.

"Do you know how to fish?"
Snow White answers yes, so Scarlet tells her to try making a fishing rod.
Snow White answers no, so Scarlet says she'll personally make a fishing rod for Snow White.

"Given thou doth intend on fabricating a fishing rod, I shall search for a suitable piece of wood."

Scarlet begins looking for wood nearby and asks Snow White how long the tree branch should be cut.

Snow White notices the branch is shorter than she expected.
Scarlet asks if it is what Snow White actually wanted.
Snow White ponders if she should use the branch for something else.

Scarlet brings over a branch with the perfect length. Snow White is very satisfied.
To make the fishing rod, she...

Snow White doesn't find anything she could use to make a fishing rod.
She gives it some further thought, and decides she can use the branch to make something else.
Snow White is good with her hands, and she manages to make a fishing rod using the metal wire and the tree branch.

Snow White passes the branch to Scarlet and tells her to sharpen one end.

"Dost thou intend on fashioning a fishing spear?"

After a while, they end up with a decent fishing spear.

*Swish* *Splash*
The fishing spear embeds itself in the bottom of the river.

"..."
"Alas, another miss."

Snow White and Scarlet continue throwing their self-made spear with all their might,
but every throw ends up with it either stuck in the riverbed from excess force or moving erratically due to poor aim.

"..."
"Perhaps we should entertain the notion of returning to a fishing rod?"

As Snow White listens to Scarlet, she stares at the fish in the river. It swims away slowly, as if mocking them.

She manages to catch a huge fish with her bare hands!

"!!!"

The fish Snow White is holding tries to writhe free from her grip.

"I had no idea thou art capable of such feats!"
"I figured I'd give it a shot, and it worked."
"..."

Despite expending so much energy earlier, the thought of having a good meal later that night gives them both a second wind, and they begin catching fish with their bare hands.
Snow White fills the pail with fish and returns to the post full of delight, discreetly wiping the drool forming on the edges of her mouth.
Hail to the King... of Fishing!

The two head to the river to begin fishing.
Snow White...

Snow White stands by the river with the fishing rod she has made.
She closes her eyes and tries to sense the movements of the fish.

A long time passes, but nothing happens.
Snow White, whose eyes are closed, can feel Scarlet nodding off behind her.
The fish also seem to have fallen asleep, as nothing is biting the rod.
It seems that fishing is more than just making a fishing rod.

Scarlet is surprised that Snow White handed the rod to her.
As she lowers the rod into the water, she proclaims that Snow White won't regret entrusting her with it.

Scarlet says that no fish will come if she doesn't move the rod, and claims they can only catch a big fish if they shake the rod.
She begins swinging the rod as she speaks.
Almost immediately, they catch something...!

"A pocket knife...?"

Scarlet has caught... a pocket knife.
She hasn't seen something like this in a long time and stares at it, forlorn.
Snow White recalls a memory with Scarlet from long ago.

That day, they were starving.
Though they had succeeded in their mission, additional supplies were taking a long time to arrive as they were in a secluded place difficult for humans to reach.

"I'm so hungry, I could eat a horse."

To a food lover like Snow White, enduring hunger is the worst form of torture imaginable.
Suddenly, Scarlet tosses a pocket knife at the birds flying by.

"!!!"

Scarlet takes the fallen bird and passes it to Snow White.

"Prithee thou not be lost in melancholy. Grill this."
"!!!"

The bird was tiny, but Snow White isn't concerned about whether it would be filling or not.
Rather, she is shocked that Scarlet is willing to kill something merely because she is hungry.
Snow White mutters, "This is so cruel." which causes Scarlet to laugh.

"So killing a tiny bird is cruel, but killing a bigger bird is perfectly okay?"
"It's not like that..."
"Do not allow thyself to be vexed thusly about death. All lives have to end."

Scarlet's nonchalance prompts Snow White to ask another question. 

"How about us?
Will we die as well?"

Scarlet chuckles.

"Flowers are fleetly fading
All things eventually come to an end."

Scarlet stared at her katana.

"This is the lesson she gave me when she became my blade."

"Flowers are fleetly fading."

Snow White utters, startling Scarlet.

"Thy memory of this still rings true?"

Snow White nods, sending a smile across Scarlet's face.

"Precisely. Nothing lasts forever, and we are no exception."

With that, Scarlet hovers the rod over the river again.
Behind her, Snow White stares at her quietly.

"We shall require wood if we are to fashion a fishing rod."
"I'll look for some."

Snow White looks around and fires her rifle at a tree that looks to be the right size.

"?!!"

The tree sways a few times before collapsing on a pile of nearby rocks.

"... I only required but a few tree branches."
"Oh... whoops."

The sight of Snow White obliterating the tree makes Scarlet feel slightly uneasy, but she feels somewhat reassured upon seeing how embarrassed Snow White seems for her slip-up. Scarlet runs over to fetch some branches from the fallen tree.

However, Scarlet is unable to make a fishing rod due to her poor crafting skills.
Feeling embarrassed, Scarlet...

Scarlet stands by the river with her sword and lightly swings it at the fish lethargically swimming by.
*Swoosh*

"Whoops."
"!!!"

The fish is cut in two and floats to the surface of the water.

"I doth believe there is validity to this idea yet. I shall swing it properly this time."

Scarlet adjusts her stance as she stands at the riverbank. Snow White is filled with a renewed sense of hope that they'll actually catch a bevy of fish, and her eyes sparkle.

However, as Scarlet swings her sword with full force,
the river is dyed a dreadful red as all the fish are sliced and diced.

"..."
"..."

Both Scarlet and Snow White stare at the massacre silently and return to the post without a word.
It might be better to do a bit of searching than relying on your colleague's sword.

"Perchance there are canned goods buried under these rocks. Hath thou considered this?"

Snow White nods and begins rummaging through the rock pile.
After they move away some rocks, some supplies hidden under the pile are gradually revealed.
Scarlet and Snow White exchange glances. Their hunch was right. Filled with a renewed sense of vigor, they begin lifting up more rocks.
Just then, Snow White feels something.

It's a parasol.
While looking at it, a memory of Dorothy resurfaces.

Back when humans lived on the surface and not in the Ark, 
Dorothy loved using the parasol that had been given to them as a gift. Supplies were plentiful then.
Nikkes don't get tanned even if they're exposed to the sun, so Snow White was curious as to why Dorothy was using the parasol.

"Why do you use that thing, anyway? It's not like we need it."

With a smile, Dorothy answered her.

"If I use this, this place won't feel as much like a battlefield. Instead, it'll feel more like a warm and sunny... Eden."
"Eden?"
"How should I put it... It makes me feel important. When the Ark is built, we'll all be sheltered safely under the same parasol."

Snow White couldn't make head or tail of what Dorothy was saying.
Will the Ark really become our Eden?
When peace is restored, will the humans want us to stay under the same parasol as them?

"Of course."

As Snow White stared at Dorothy, her expression was full of such hope for the future, that she couldn't bring herself to refute her in any way.

"Oh, a parasol... Dorothy will be most smitten with this." 

Scarlet proclaims as she approaches Snow White.
Snow White nods quietly.
Both of them feel this will be the perfect gift for Dorothy, who's doing her best to be a fine leader.
They bring the parasol back to the post.

Rapunzel appears before Snow White, who's on her way to explore the church.

"Come with me today.
I've been to the suburb."

Snow White nods.
Snow White and Rapunzel head to the outskirts and gaze at the structures demolished by Raptures. They attempt to find a recognizable structure they can check out.

The factory seems to be a former refuge for the humans. Although some parts of the building have collapsed, there are some blankets and canned goods scattered around.
Rapunzel and Snow White venture further into the factory.

Snow White and Rapunzel go to the apartment buildings to look for daily necessities, but most of them have been completely obliterated from Rapture attacks.
There are only 3 houses they can still enter.
Snow White...

The inside of the factory is littered with all manner of supplies,
but the cans of food are either emptied or spoiled. Everything else is unsalvageable.
Snow White and Rapunzel want to continue looking for things they can use, so they...

When they break the locked door open and walk in, they see canned goods and other supplies all placed in a neat pile, although there aren't many of them.
This must be a room that had been used as storage. Snow White and Rapunzel begin gathering up the canned goods.
In the midst of their scavenging, Snow White discovers a book under the couch.

"What is this?"

There are matches, extinguished candles. pictures of people hanging in the room.
A line is written on the wall.
"May you rest in peace."

"This must be a place where they mourn the dead."

The two look around for a while and...

The two are elated, as they didn't expect to find such a major haul.
As Rapunzel looks at the canned goods, she remembers how the atmosphere at the post has been fairly gloomy lately. Dorothy has also been rather morose as well. Rapunzel suggests that they make some dishes and give everyone else a pleasant surprise.
Snow White agrees with the idea.
Rapunzel...

The book under the couch is a dirty magazine.

"Ugh, what is this?"

Rapunzel walks over and stares at the magazine.

"Whoa, I thought this series ended already!"

Her eyes gleam as she speaks.
Snow White suddenly remembers a previously forgotten memory of her, Rapunzel, and Red Hood.

Rapunzel steps forward confidently, claiming she has always loved cooking even as a human.
As Snow White watches Rapunzel, she feels a little anxious.

*Gurgle, gurgle, gurgle.*
An unknown substance boils in the pot.
What was once delicious food is now a disastrous pile of black mush. It can no longer even be considered food.

"What in the world did you put in there?"
"I... I just made it the way I did before..."

Snow White is speechless. She snatches the final can of food before Rapunzel can destroy that as well, and returns to the post.
Become A Master In Your Own Kitchen Tomorrow?
Don't trust everything your friends say.

Rapunzel says she happens to have a cookbook handy that she'll follow.
She announces she'll use this canned food to make something delicious, and goes out to start a fire.
As Snow White watches Rapunzel, her anxiety slowly builds.

*Gurgle, gurgle, gurgle.*
An appetizing soup boils in the huge pot.
Its aroma fills the factory, and Snow White begins to drool.

"Can I have a taste?"
"Hehe. Of course!"

Rapunzel confidently ladles some soup into a small can and passes it to Snow White.
Snow White puts a spoonful of soup in her mouth.

"!!!"

She is filled with pure ecstasy.

"How is it? Does it taste okay?"
"It's wonderful."

Rapunzel's mood improves when she sees Snow White's obvious delight.
With the big pot and canned goods in tow, they return to the post triumphant.
Become A Master In Your Own Kitchen Today!

"What are you showing Snow White?!"

Rapunzel covers Snow White's eyes.
Not being particular about her reading material, Red Hood has just passed a dirty magazine to Snow White.

Rapunzel blushes and urges Red Hood to throw away this smut. Undeterred, Red Hood continues to tease Rapunzel with the racy magazine.
While Snow White watches them argue, she realizes the animosity between the Red Hood and Rapunzel has given way to real friendship.

"You're not the slightest bit shy about reading this kind of stuff?"
"Oh, you still remember that?"

Snow White nods,
while Rapunzel smiles.

"How could I forget? After going through that, I don't think anyone else can make me feel embarrassed ever again."

Rapunzel takes the dirty magazine from Snow White.

"I can read things even more salacious than this now."
"Red Hood would be shocked if she saw me now, wouldn't she?"
"Actually, she's probably over the moon that she managed to influence me."
Rapunzel returns the magazine to Snow White.

"I kept feeling like Red Hood was embarrassing me on purpose, so I was annoyed."
"But now, I kinda miss it."

Rapunzel stops talking and begins collecting the rest of the scattered canned food.
Meanwhile, Snow White watches her quietly.
A Friendship She Misses Despite the Embarrassment

Rapunzel and Snow White light the candles with the matches on the floor and pray for a while.
They then walk out of the room and open the locked door.

Rapunzel places the photo frame they got from the apartment building among the pictures on the floor and lights the candles with a match.
Once all the candles in the room are lit, Rapunzel kneels down quietly.
Without a word, Snow White stands back and watches.

Snow White asks.

"Why are you doing this?"
"What?"
"They're already dead."

Rapunzel answers.

"Death is not the end."
"The marks these people made during their lives will not disappear simply because they are no longer with us."
"Everything truly ends only when everyone who remembers them is gone."

Rapunzel stands up and looks at Snow White.

"So, I decide to remember."
"I don't want them to be forgotten, for everything to come to an end and rob them of all meaning."
"..."
"So I will keep praying to remember the precious lives they used to lead. I will acknowledge their deaths and bid them farewell."

Death is not the end.
The real end happens when one's existence is forgotten.
Snow White falls into deep thought.
She has never thought of it that way.

Rapunzel looks at Snow White, who is lost in thought, and kneels once again to pray.
While Snow White watches Rapunzel pray, she asks...

"Then how do we bid someone farewell?"
"Look them in the eyes say to them..."
"Be well."

Snow White leaves Rapunzel behind and begins exploring the factory again. She smells the familiar scent of flowers.
Snow White follows the scent and finds a door toward the back.
Snow White...

Snow White takes out the dried white flower she got from the apartments and opens the door.
As the door opens, a sea of white flowers greets Snow White.
She knows the name of these flowers.
They remind Snow White of her.
Memories of her come rushing back. Memories Snow White has been wanting to forget.

She was always fond of her.
Being together with her was always a happy experience.
Snow White was never happier than when they had chatted in a prairie full of flowers just like these. 

"This flower has the same name as you."
"Yes. That's where I got my name."

Snow White loved that flower ever since.

"But now, it seems like... this flower is more like you than me."

No.
This flower still resembles her.

"The pure,"
The purest,
"strong,"
strongest,
"and lovely"
and loveliest
"Snow White."
Liliweiss.

Snow White runs toward the field of liliweiss before her.
After staring at the flowers for a while as if in a daze, she sits down and caresses them.

"Can I...
go and see you?"
"... Please."

The sky turns red. Snow White continues to cradle the liliweiss in her arms,
even when Rapunzel comes looking for her after praying.

Walking into the house on the left, the two find the posters of the Ark and lots of lottery tickets scattered inside.
The lottery tickets have Try Again printed on them. Amongst the pile, there is a cookbook.

On the pages, sentences such as Recipes Anyone Can Learn! Become A Master In Your Own Kitchen Today! can be made out. Rapunzel says it would be nice if they can find food and make some dishes to bring back to the post.
Snow White asks Rapunzel if she needs the cookbook. Rapunzel says...

"There's no harm in having a cookbook."

Rapunzel says.
Snow White agrees with her.
Feeling they won't be able to find anything else in the house, they decide to...

"When it comes to cooking, all you need is intuition."

Rapunzel says.
Snow White decides to believe her.
Feeling they won't be able to find anything else in the house, they decide to...

They come to the house in the middle and see a bunch of empty cans piled up neatly in a corner of the empty room. It seems that someone else has been here.
While most of the doors are either open or broken, they find one door that is tightly closed.
They...

For now, looking for supplies and food is the top priority.
Upon picking up the familiar smell of death coming from inside, they decide not to open the door.

There's a bed in the room.
On the bed lie two bodies, their fingers intertwined.
Snow White and Rapunzel wordlessly look at the photo frame on the bedside table.
A couple smiles happily in the picture.

"Seems like they're a couple."
"..."

After looking at the picture for a while, Rapunzel says she wants to mourn the deceased and decides to take the photo frame with her.
Feeling they won't be able to find anything else in the house, they decide to...

The house on the right is entirely empty.
Rapunzel posits the former residents must have taken refuge somewhere else.
Snow White looks at the empty room and discovers a dried white flower that has fallen on the ground.

There's a buzzing in her ear, then a voice rings out.
"This flower is more like you than me."

"Snow White?"

Rapunzel's voice brings Snow White back to reality.
Despite Rapunzel's concern, Snow White insists everything is fine and tells her not to worry. Snow White then suggests they continue their search. 
Rapunzel agrees and walks away, while Snow White...
Snow White feels an unprecedented wave of emotions and surreptitiously takes the dried white flower.
Feeling that keeping the flower will bring back some unpleasant memories, Snow White decides to avert her gaze.
Feeling they won't be able to find anything else in the house, they decide to...
Believing there might not be many supplies or food available at the apartments, they instead decide to check out the factory.

Snow White walks toward the field.
The sun's rays cascade across the peaceful meadow. At the far end there is a stone coffin, encircled by towering trees.
It is there that she slumbers.

“...”

Snow White gazes from afar, half in a daze.

She still doesn't have the courage to walk forward.
Snow White goes back in hopes of finding something that will give her courage.
Snow White holds the memory capsule. Although Snow White isn't confident about maintaining her composure whilst facing her, she musters the courage to step forward.

There is a buzzing sound, then a voice rings out.

"You're Snow White, aren't you?"
"Hello."
"I'm Li..."

Snow White remains where she is.
She doesn't have the courage to move forward and meet her.
I'm not ready.
I don't deserve to see her.
I haven't achieved anything at all.
I can't even remember her face, or her name. How can I possibly face her ■■?

Not yet.
It's not yet time.
I can't face her ■■ yet.
Snow White fails to take another step.
After taking that one step towards her,
Snow White stops.
The Step She Failed to Take
Snow White can only walk forward when she remembers her name.

Snow White looks at the liliweiss flower. It was Liliweiss's favorite.

"... I have to go."

At long last,
Snow White makes that step she failed to take before.

Leave With the Flower
A coffin lies on the vast meadow, surrounded by soaring trees.
Liliweiss.
The first Nikke.
The leader of the Goddess Squad.
Snow White's hero, who was stronger and more beautiful than anyone else.

"..."

After a long journey, Snow White finally arrives before the slumbering Liliweiss.
Bunches of flowers adorn her grave. A grief-stricken Snow White salutes.

"... Hello."

Liliweiss, my hero.
Never did I feel I was in danger, so long as you were there on the battlefield with me.
Never once did I retreat from anything.
My honor was your honor,
and your happiness was mine.
So, I didn't want to accept the fact that you won't be joining me on my future journey.
I didn't want to accept the fact that I won't be able to see you laugh once again.
But it's time to say farewell.
You gave me a mission.
That mission alone proves you once existed in this world.
It will be the reason this world remembers you and your great achievements.
So please... My sister, my colleague, my soulmate.
My hero.

"Be well."

Snow White places the Liliweiss flower on Liliweiss's coffin.
Finally, she bids her farewell.

Snow White decides to check the surroundings.
She slowly realizes that she has never given this place a proper once-over.
As she started to move in the direction where she can see the Ark,

*Clang*

Snow White accidentally kicks something.

"??"

She looks down and finds a dog tag.
Yet another memory that had remained buried for so long resurfaces.

Snow White remembers that person she has previously forgotten.
He said he was a mercenary, but he didn't seem like the military type.
He was the man who became our leader, who claimed that he would suppress the Raptures.

Commander.

When did it begin?
His bluntness and impertinence gave way to tenderness, and he began treating us like humans...

"I hope you don't get hurt again."

Liliweiss kissed his dog tag.
